newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire opposition severs contacts with Mobutu.
newsitem.headline: Zaire opposition severs contacts with Mobutu.

text.p: The radical Zairean opposition of Etienne Tshisekedi said on Friday it had severed all contacts with President Mobutu Sese Seko after he kept Kengo wa Dondo in the post of prime minister at the head of a crisis government.

"The UDPS (Union for Democracy and Social Progress) is breaking all contact with Mr Mobutu. Mr Mobutu must assume alone the consequences of his acts, and history will judge him severely," UDPS secretary general Adrien Phongo Kunda said.

Phongo said the UDPS would hold a major meeting on January 4 at which it would unveil a plan of action. "The widespread generalised action which will develop across the country will force the dictatorship to flee," he told a news conference.
The secretary general of the Solidarity trade union, Steve Mbikayi, told Reuters that trades unionists were preparing to launch a nationwide general strike on January 4.
Mobutu, who returned home on December 17 after four months absence in Europe for cancer surgery and rest, announced a crisis government on Tuesday to deal with a rebel revolt in the east.
Tshisekedi, named prime minister by a national conference in 1992 but shunted aside in favour of a Mobutu appointee a year later, has never accepted Kengo's 1994 appointment to the job.
Tshisekedi's supporters, who are in the majority in the teeming poorer neighbourhoods of the capital, had expected him to get the job back in the latest government reshuffle.
Tshisekedi held a "reconciliation" meeting with Mobutu in southern France, shortly before the veteran leader returned. It is not the first time his UDPS has broken contacts with Mobutu.
